short: The Notitia Dignitatum, compiled around 400 CE, lists every civil office and military unit of the late Roman state in unmatched detail.
full:
Compiled in stages around 400 CE, with its eastern section largely complete by 401 and its western section still being revised into the 420s, the Notitia Dignitatum is a register of every senior civil and military post in the Roman Empire, listing officials, provinces, dioceses, army units and their stations. It survives only through medieval copies of a lost original, illustrated with the emblem of each office.

No comparable document survives from any other period of Roman history, and its lists of military units stationed along the Rhine, Danube and eastern frontiers remain a primary source for reconstructing the late Roman army's order of battle. Historians treat it cautiously, since the eastern and western sections reflect different dates and some entries plainly went unrevised as posts and units changed.
